matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character; many puzzles can be solved this way without altering other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is invalid, before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move a stick from one numeral to another without first checking if moving it inside a single numeral could resolve the mismatch.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, verify that each resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or operator; any shape that does not correspond to a valid symbol indicates an invalid move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal line after taking a stick from X, which no longer matches any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; when moving a diagonal from X or V, ensure the remaining part still forms a valid character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a diagonal stick from X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X and leaving a lone slash, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If intra‑character moves fail, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character; this can change numerals or operators to achieve a valid equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from III to V to turn XV into XVI and III into II, as in the correct solution.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides after any transformation; an equation that looks syntactically correct must also be arithmetically true.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a visually correct equation like IXIV = XV - II without checking that IXIV is not a standard numeral or that the arithmetic holds.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the '=', ensure that after the move the equation still contains exactly one valid equality sign (two horizontal sticks).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is moved from or to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=', turning it into a minus sign, and not creating a new '=' elsewhere, leaving the equation without a proper equality sign.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a vertical stick to create an extra I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick becomes free after modifying a character and can be used to form an additional numeral.
matchstick.example: Leaving a stray vertical stick unused after converting '+' to '-', resulting in an incomplete equation.

matchstick.title: Swap equality and subtraction operators
matchstick.principle: When both '=' and '-' appear, you can move a horizontal stick from the equality sign to the subtraction sign (or vice versa) to swap them, ensuring the equation still has exactly one '=' sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains both '=' and '-', consider swapping them by moving a single horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-', turning the original '=' into '-', and the original '-' into '=', but forgetting to keep a single '=' in the final equation.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After moving sticks, ensure each multi‑character numeral follows standard Roman numeral rules (ordering, subtractive notation); a sequence of valid symbols is not enough if the combined numeral is nonstandard.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick relocation, before accepting the solution, check each numeral string for standard form.
matchstick.example: Creating IXIV, which is not a standard Roman numeral, even though each character I, X, I, V is individually valid.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler fixes within a single symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate possible intra‑character stick relocations for each numeral/operator before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: Diagonal sticks are treated as interchangeable with vertical sticks, leading to leftover diagonal pieces that don't form any numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When taking a diagonal from X or V, ensure the remaining part still matches a valid Roman numeral; otherwise avoid that move.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual validity of symbols and forgets to check numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any proposed move, compute the numeric values of both sides and confirm they are equal before finalizing.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operator symbols as independent and forgets the requirement of exactly one equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When swapping operators, verify that the final equation still contains exactly one valid '=' sign.

matchstick.description: Creating nonstandard Roman numeral forms (e.g., IXIV) that are not valid according to standard Roman numeral rules
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks only individual character validity, not the combined numeral syntax.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, validate each multi‑character numeral against standard Roman numeral conventions (order, subtractive notation).
